move.title: Tender cookies, a sweet filling
move.body: Alfajores are Argentina's favorite cookie: two tender, crumbly cookies made with cornstarch, stuck together with dulce de leche and rolled in coconut. Today you'll cream butter and sugar, roll and cut even rounds, and bake them pale so they stay soft.

callback.body: Brown butter cookies spread into chewy rounds. Alfajores are rolled and cut, and cornstarch keeps them short and crumbly so they hold a filling without spreading.

why.title: Why cornstarch
why.body: Cornstarch has no gluten. Using lots of it in place of flour makes a cookie that's tender and melts in your mouth.

why.title: Creaming
why.body: Beating soft butter with powdered sugar makes a smooth, light dough that rolls out without cracking.

why.title: Why chill the dough
why.body: Soft dough sticks to everything. Half an hour in the fridge firms the butter so the dough rolls and cuts cleanly.

why.title: Bake them pale
why.body: Alfajores should stay light on top. They're done when the bottoms are just golden. Browned cookies turn hard and dry.

wrong.sign: The dough cracks when you roll it
wrong.fix: It's too cold. Let it sit 5 minutes, then roll again.

wrong.sign: The dough sticks to the counter
wrong.fix: It's too warm. Chill it 10 more minutes and dust the counter with flour.

wrong.sign: The cookies broke when you filled them
wrong.fix: They were still warm. Let them cool all the way first.
Take the next pan out 2 minutes sooner.

choices: Lots of cornstarch, which has no gluten
quiz.explain: No gluten means a soft, crumbly cookie.

choices: So it rolls and cuts cleanly
quiz.explain: Cold butter keeps it from sticking.

choices: Pale on top, bottoms just golden

steps.text: Beat the soft butter and powdered sugar in the large bowl with the wooden spoon.
Add the egg and vanilla. Beat until smooth.
steps.look: Smooth, with no streaks of egg.

steps.text: Wash your hands with soap, and throw away the eggshell.
Whisk the cornstarch, flour, and baking powder in the medium bowl.
Stir the dry mix into the butter until a soft dough forms. Press it into a flat disk.
steps.tip: Don't taste the raw dough. It has raw egg and flour.

steps.text: Cover the dough and chill it in the fridge.
Heat the oven to 350°F. Line the sheet pan with parchment.
Flour the counter. Roll the dough ¼ inch thick and cut 24 rounds with the cutter.
steps.tip: Press the scraps together and roll them again.

steps.text: Set the rounds on the pan, 1 inch apart. Bake until the bottoms are just golden.
steps.look: Pale on top, and just golden underneath.

steps.text: With an adult and oven mitts, take out the pan. Lift one cookie with the spatula and look underneath.
steps.tip: Still white underneath? Bake 2 more minutes.

steps.text: Turn off the oven. Move the cookies to the rack and let them cool all the way.
steps.tip: Warm cookies break when you fill them.

steps.text: Spread a spoonful of dulce de leche on 12 cookies with the butter knife. Top each with another cookie.
steps.look: 12 sandwiches, filling right to the edge.

steps.text: Pour the coconut onto the plate. Roll the edge of each sandwich in it.
steps.look: A ring of coconut around each one.
